segments.caption: Wellington. 290 balls. 136 runs.
KL Rahul's 13th Test hundred, in his first ever Test in New Zealand.
And it made him the first Indian opener with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries.
But his career has never been a straight line.
71 Tests. 123 innings. Every bar here is one of them.
The gold line is his average over his last ten innings. Watch it rise, crash, and rise again.
It began with 3 and 1 on debut, at Melbourne.
A week later, a hundred at Sydney.
In 2017, he made seven fifties in a row, equalling a world record.
And at Chennai, he was out for 199.
Then the line fell off a cliff.
From August 2018: 22 innings, at an average of 23.
Take away one great hundred at the Oval, and it drops to 17.
In 2019 he was dropped, and didn't play another Test for almost two years.
He came back in England, and made a hundred at Lord's. Then another at Centurion.
Moved down the order, he made a third, again at Centurion, batting at number six.
But the middle order never really suited him. 27 there. 39 as an opener.
Back at the top, something changed.
Since Leeds 2025: 22 innings, five hundreds, and an average of 55.
So what changed?
He isn't scoring faster. His strike rate has barely moved, from 57 to 50.
He's staying longer. In the slump, he lasted 41 balls per dismissal. Now, 112.
The biggest change is at the very start.
Until 2019, two in every five innings ended inside his first 20 balls.
Since Leeds, it has happened once in 22.
Then there's the new ball, an opener's real test.
In the first 20 overs, he used to average around 25. Since Leeds: 58.
Now, the strangest part.
He averages 42 at home, and 35 away. Yet 10 of his 13 hundreds came away.
The answer is conversion. At home, 3 of his 14 fifty-plus scores became hundreds. Away, 10 of 20.
One more pattern.
The first time India bat in a Test, he averages 43, with 11 of his 13 hundreds.
Second time around: 29.
4,424 runs. A career of crashes, and comebacks.
At 34, the best version of KL Rahul may be the one batting right now.
Beyond The Scoreboard.
